name: Career Readiness and Modern Youth Apprenticeship (CRMYA)
org: NYC Public Schools with CareerWise New York
what_you_do: 9th and 10th graders take career readiness classes. Juniors can apply for a paid apprenticeship. It lasts 2 to 3 years. You work at a workplace while you finish high school. You earn a state-registered credential.
who_can_apply: Students at participating NYC public high schools. Juniors apply for the apprenticeship.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Pay rate is not stated on the page.
duration: 2 to 3 year apprenticeship starting junior year
deadline_text: Dates are not stated. Juniors apply during the school year; ask your school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school if it participates. Juniors apply for apprenticeships through the program. The page does not list an application link.
notes: Only at participating schools; the page does not list which ones. Apprentices attend school mornings Monday to Thursday and all day Friday, and work Monday to Thursday afternoons. Apprenticeships are registered with the NYS Department of Labor. Paid work for people under 18 in New York needs working papers (employment certificate). See permit.html?state=ny for the exact permit and steps.
